detector: classical baseline (local-contrast threshold, connected components, uniformity rejection)

detector_params.note: threshold is a fraction of the scene median, not an absolute level; it adapts to scene brightness but not to scene contrast

radiometry.reason: integer dtype: these are digital numbers, not calibrated sigma-nought. Calibration to linear or dB requires the product's own calibration LUT, which is not derivable from the pixel values
radiometry.detection_assumes: a darkness threshold on amplitude. On a dB raster the ordering is preserved, so the threshold still selects dark pixels; on a raster whose scale has been misidentified and converted, it selects the wrong ones and reports a confident detection

land_rejection.note: regions more than 50% on land are rejected; a region straddling the shoreline is kept, because oil does reach a coast and discarding a landfall detection would be worse than the false positive it guards against

multi_region_note: Single region in this scene; top-level geometry and regions[0] agree.

agreement_with_truth_mask.note: Available because this is a synthetic case with a generator truth mask. On real imagery no such label exists.

measurement_note: Geometry measured in local azimuthal-equidistant metres centred on the scene at 18.90 N: 410.9 m east-west against 434.4 m north-south, rather than the manifest's single 433.59 m figure, which treats a pixel as square and overstates area by about 5% at this latitude. Distances and directions from the scene centre are true, which is what area, axis lengths and bearing require. This is not a full reprojection into EPSG:32643 - over a scene one degree across the difference is far below the detector's own boundary uncertainty. Axis lengths are 2-sigma extents along the principal axes.
boundary_note: SAR darkness is not proof of oil. Look-alikes (low wind, biogenic films) dampen backscatter too; detection confidence is kept separate from source confidence throughout.
